An ideal scoring system for this competition would be one that takes into account the complexity of the games, as well as the number of players each player competes against in each game. Here is a scoring system that meets these requirements:

1. For each game, each player receives a score equal to the average complexity of the game rounded to two decimal places. For example, for a game with a complexity of 2.2, each player would receive a score of 2.20.
2. For each game, each player receives a bonus score equal to the number of players they beat in that game. For example, if there are 12 players in the competition and a player wins a game in which they compete against 4 other players, they would receive a bonus score of 4.
3. The total score for each player is the sum of their scores and bonus scores across all 9 games.

This scoring system rewards players for performing well in more complex games and against more players. It also ensures that each player has an equal opportunity to earn points in each game, regardless of the particular opponents they face.
